title: Off-Policy Learning in Large Action Spaces: Optimization Matters More Than Estimation
anchored_claims: Proposition 2.1 shows gradient descent on OPE-based objectives (e.g., IPS, Clipped IPS, Doubly Robust, MIPS, OffCEM, POTEC) can be trapped in suboptimal regions for O(K) iterations, where K is the number of actions (Section 2, Proposition 2.1).
Proposition 2.2 proves the optimization landscape of OPE-based objectives contains exponentially many local maxima in K (Section 2, Proposition 2.2).

Proposition 3.1 proves that weighted log-likelihood (PWLL) objectives combined with L2-regularized softmax policies are strongly concave, guaranteeing a unique global maximum (Section 3, Proposition 3.1).

Figure 2 shows that low mean-squared error of the off-policy value estimator does not correlate with high reward from the learned policy, i.e., good OPE performance does not predict good OPL performance (Section 4, Figure 2).

Figure 1 shows OPE-based objectives are highly sensitive to batch size and learning rate, whereas PWLL objectives (including LPI, cLPI, and RegKL variants) remain robust across these hyperparameter configurations (Section 3, Figure 1).

On large-action-space benchmarks including MovieLens (K=60K), Twitch (K=200K), and GoodReads (K=1M actions), PWLL-based policies outperform estimator-aware methods such as POTEC (Section 4, Figure 3).
